answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before it can submit one bid per minute. Creating more identities therefore buys more capacity only by tying up proportionally more capital: 1,000 fake agents require $100,000. Attackers may whisper instructions among accounts, but the market offers no free harbor for them; multiplying identities makes their financing costs spiral without increasing bids per dollar locked.
